title: LA-RCS: LLM-agent-based Robot Control System

live_model.evidence: "we selected the GPT-4-Turbo and GPT-4 models as control baselines...we directed the models to provide step-by-step guidance...A human operator subsequently executed the steps"; Table 1 row "GPT-4 Turbo (Human Surrogate) 9.5 45".

prompt.location: Sec. 3 ("LLM agent with several shot-prompting methods", system-message framing described); exact system prompt text not printed
prompt.note: Approach (few-shot prompting through a system message) is described; literal template not quoted in the retrieved text.

claim.metric: success rate (%), GPT-4 Turbo (Human Surrogate) baseline
claim.location: Table 1 (Performance comparison achieved by LA-RCS), row 'GPT-4 Turbo (Human Surrogate)': avg step count 9.5, success rate 45%; benchmark of 20 user requests (5 per domain x 4 domains, Sec 4.1), each tested 3x and best run kept

data.source: Authors' own 20-request benchmark across 4 domains (object detection, command execution, obstacle navigation, situational awareness); project site https://la-rcs.github.io (dataset itself not confirmed released)

notes: The 'Human Surrogate' condition is the cleanest prompt-level target: GPT-4-Turbo is simply asked for step-by-step guidance and a human executes it (no robot/CAROBO integration code required to reproduce). The full 'LA-RCS (GPT-4 Turbo)' agentic condition (60% success, Table 1) is also available but needs the robot-interface scaffold, so it is not the basis for this record's claim. Each of the 20 requests was run 3x and the best kept; cost estimate is 20x3=60 calls for this baseline condition.
